critical_code_review_comments: ThemeEditor cleanup effect at AdminBranding.jsx:27 uses `JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('nk_theme') || 'null') || initial` — if the user previews a preset and navigates away without saving, the UI reverts to the saved theme on next mount. OK. But if two admin tabs are open and one saves, the other's `initial` prop becomes stale (it was captured from /admin/site at mount). Minor.

AdminSections `blank(type)` seeds id=null and the row is given data-testid key `new-${i}` in the list. Server generates a real id on save. Fine, but the delete-section flow has no confirm dialog; a single misclick on sec-delete-<i> immediately removes an unsaved custom section with no undo. Consider adding window.confirm or a staged state.

AdminFooter `save()` silently filters out link rows with empty label OR empty url (line 39). Users can lose work without feedback. Consider toasting 'N incomplete link(s) removed' or disabling footer-save until all partial rows are complete.

clean_sections (server.py:270) accepts a user-supplied `id` for custom sections and only replaces it if blank OR colliding with another seen id OR colliding with a built-in. If a client sends `id='random'` for a brand-new text section it will stick, which is fine, but there is no uniqueness check against other custom sections already saved in DB — only within the submitted list. Not a security issue (sections are display-only).

ThemeIn validates hex per-field with regex but there is no contrast check — admins can save brand=#000000 ink=#000000 and make the whole store unreadable. Non-blocking but a soft 'low contrast between brand and ink' warning would be helpful.

site.js `reloadSite()` applies the theme every time; on cold start it ALSO runs applyCachedTheme() from localStorage. If an admin changed the theme on another browser, the old browser momentarily shows cached theme then flashes to new one on first /site response — acceptable.

HomeSections.jsx Cta only renders when BOTH button_text AND link are set; AdminSections lets you save a section with only one of the two but the frontend silently drops the button. Consider blocking save with a validation toast when exactly one is filled.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (admin home tiles, branding, theme live preview, sections editor + public render, footer, 13-section jump, shop/vendors/vault/wallet regression — zero console errors)
